SMTO-CFG-0071 — SMTO couldn't find one of its built-in instructions

GUID: 9e9810d2-4918-42c8-8189-604006ab827d
Slug: prompt-not-found
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO looked for a built-in instruction it gives the Agent behind the scenes and couldn't find it in its own files or saved copies, so the step that needed it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for running tasks to finish, then open Settings › Setup › Server updates, select Check for updates, then Update server. Or run the installer again. A missing built-in instruction usually means SMTO's program files are incomplete or come from different versions.
  2. If someone replaced or edited SMTO's built-in instruction files directly, instead of using the Prompt Editor, ask them to put the original files back. SMTO only finds instructions under the names its own files use.
  3. Open the conversation and check what the task already finished before asking again. Start a fresh request rather than reusing an old one. Part of the task may have run before it stopped, and repeating it blindly could do that work twice.

What success looks like

  • New tasks run to the end without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your SMTO version, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend an old request copied from before the update; start a new one from the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PromptFetcher found no registered catalog entry, active stored template or checked-in default for the requested prompt key, or a template upsert could not read back the record it had just written.

What this means

  • Prompt lookup finds neither a stored template nor a checked-in default, or a template write cannot read back its expected record. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Prompt lookup finds neither a stored template nor a checked-in default, or a template write cannot read back its expected record.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact template key, stored record and built-in fallback; a post-write absence needs store diagnosis.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the requested key exists in this build's prompt catalog (agent_runtime/prompts) and in any custom defaults path; reinstall to repair a mixed or partial installation. For a failed upsert readback, check the prompt store (userprompts.db or the Server's prompts store) for write failures in the Server log.
  • Refresh the prompt list and select an existing template or save the intended new template.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended template resolves from a supported source and renders with its required inputs.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
